column1: # Key of Charles V to Ferrante Gonzaga, Monzón, 11 August 1542 (Biblioteca Estense, Lettera K, sfasc. IV, cc. 109-110), found by Prabal Gupta (repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757, CC BY 4.0).

# A base sign is a consonant, and a small digit above it adds the vowel: 1 to 5 run a, e, i, o, u, and 6 to 9 and 0 run a, e, i, o, u again for a second consonant. A sign with no digit is a single letter.
# The label names the shape of a sign in transcription.txt, not a value. "none" is a sign with no digit. The column uses gives the count in this letter.

# g with 6 gives "ha", not "ca": its four uses are all in "haver", and no cipher word of the letter needs "ca". c with no digit gives d at the end of a syllable (seguridad, necesidad, podrá) and l elsewhere.
# s marks a doubled or palatal consonant between two vowels: ss, ll, rr or ñ. X, and g with no digit, are nulls.
